red.scope: Four real Git merge entries plus controlled remote merge had no native ownership refusal; unrelated legacy source still merges. Initial fixture NOT NULL errors were corrected before the observed RED.

green.scope: 6new publication cases, task input invalidation and legacy Git tools; real fixture Git and SQLite, controlled remote transport, no model.

limits: Does not implement native publication, external effect reconciliation or a writable-source execution domain.
Preflight ownership check is not a cross-process lock or proof against first native admission racing an already-started legacy merge. That remains required in the full publication cutover.
No new wheel or complete global suite for this guard; owner explicitly requested commit, push and pause.

documented_definitions.docstring: Reject legacy merge of native-owned tasks or registered physical sources, including another task/project alias; no historical approval grants publication authority.

Merge a pull request.

If ``FORGEJO_API_URL`` is set and the PR has a ``forgejo_pr_index``,
calls the Forgejo merge API.  Otherwise performs a local
``git merge --no-ff``.
Then marks the branch as merged and updates the PR status.
Native-owned tasks and source identities are rejected before either
effect; a historical PR label cannot authorize their publication.
Create two real local commits and historical PR metadata, without an accepted native candidate.
Actual Git must stay unchanged despite a legacy approved label or a PR with another task/project identity.
An unavailable local clone or an ambient Forgejo setting cannot turn a native task's legacy status into remote authority.
A native admission in a different physical source does not remove remaining legacy functionality.
